```sql
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       t.revenue,
       t.order_count,
       t.last_order_at
  FROM customers c
  JOIN (
        SELECT o.customer_id,
               sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
               count(*)           AS order_count,
               max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
          FROM orders o
         WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
         GROUP BY o.customer_id
        HAVING max(o.created_at) >= %(from)s
           AND max(o.created_at) <  %(to)s
       ) t ON t.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
 ORDER BY t.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

Omzet, aantal orders en laatste orderdatum komen nu uit één aggregatie over `orders`, in plaats van twee aparte CTE-scans. Omdat `created_at` NOT NULL is, levert `max(created_at)` precies dezelfde waarde als `DISTINCT ON … ORDER BY created_at DESC`. Daardoor verdwijnt de nested loop die de HashAggregate 9799 keer herscande (48 miljoen weggefilterde rijen), en kan de planner gewoon een hash join met `customers` gebruiken.
